tone_statements.citation: Adoumacho, Jessé-Joël, Tychique Longbo, Guy-Florent Matchi & Kenneth S. Olson. 2020. Précis d'orthographe du ngbugu [Orthography Statement for Ngbugu]. Bangui: ACATBA et SIL International. 26 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 86801; issued 2020-03).
tone_statements.quote: Nous avons identifié trois tons ponctuels phonémiques en ngbugu : haut [á], moyen [ā] et bas [à]. Les tons modulés, en ngbugu, sont des combinaisons de tons ponctuels, par ex. : [vōtàá] trois (ton montant), [mīndúù] cinq (ton descendant). Il existe aussi des tons ponctuels longs qu’on analyse comme une séquence de tons ponctuels, par ex. : [zòò] longtemps. [...] Nous avons constaté des oppositions tonales entre des mots, par ex. [kú] punaise, [kū] cuisse, [kù] plaie (v. tableau ci-dessous). Comme il y a plusieurs paires minimales tonales, on écrit tous les tons.
tone_statements.translation: We have identified three phonemic level tones in Ngbugu: high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]. Contour tones in Ngbugu are combinations of level tones, e.g. [vōtàá] 'three' (rising tone), [mīndúù] 'five' (falling tone). There are also long level tones, which are analysed as a sequence of level tones, e.g. [zòò] 'a long time'. [...] We have found tonal oppositions between words, e.g. [kú] 'bedbug', [kū] 'thigh', [kù] 'wound' (see table below). Since there are several tonal minimal pairs, all tones are written.
tone_statements.locator: §3 'Les tons' and §3.1, p. 8; grammatical tone §3.2 p. 9
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 level (H, M, L); contours = sequences of levels

tone_statements.citation: Longbo, Tychique & Simon Bangonale. 2017. Azə̈ dɨ̈ mbëtï la ma Ngbûgu = Guide de transition à la lecture et à l’écriture en ngbugu (Basse-Kotto). 3ème édition. Bangui: ACATBA et SIL International. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 88545.)
tone_statements.quote: N.B.: Le ngbugu est une langue tonale, c'est-à-dire, chaque syllabe a sa hauteur tonale propre. Il y a des mots où seulement une différence de la hauteur tonale change le sens du mot. ... L’orthographe ngbugu marque le ton sur les voyelles. En ngbugu, il y a 3 ( trois ) possibilités de marquer les tons: Quand une voyelle se prononce avec un ton haut, elle est surmontée d’un « ^ ». Exemple: ngâ, ngôlô. Quand elle se prononce avec un ton moyen, elle est surmontée d’un « .. ». Exemple: ngötö, bä, bë Dans le cas où le ton est bas, il ne s’écrit pas. Exemple: nda, bolo, gbudu
tone_statements.translation: N.B.: Ngbugu is a tone language, that is, each syllable has its own tonal pitch. There are words where only a difference in pitch changes the meaning of the word. ... Ngbugu orthography marks tone on the vowels. In Ngbugu there are 3 (three) ways of marking the tones: when a vowel is pronounced with a high tone it carries a circumflex, e.g. ngâ, ngôlô. When it is pronounced with a mid tone it carries a diaeresis, e.g. ngötö, bä, bë. When the tone is low it is not written, e.g. nda, bolo, gbudu.
tone_statements.summary: Literacy primer: three tones high (^), mid (¨), low (unmarked), one per syllable; Leçon 18 treats rising/falling as low-high / high-low written over two identical vowels (Vötaâ, Groô).

sources.citation: Walsh, Michael J. (1983). Linguistics sound archiving. In Sound archives: a guide to their establishment and development. International Association of Sound Archives. pp. 147-161.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: General chapter on running a linguistic sound archive (field of study, role of the archive, data to collect, collecting priorities, fieldwork, documentation, staffing, equipment, running costs). Examples are Australian Aboriginal and New Guinea languages only. Banda, Ngbugu, the Central African Republic, tone, stress, accent and pitch are never mentioned; the only phonology reference is generic ('the sounds of the language.. phonology, lexicon, morphology', p. 2). Nothing usable for the catalog entry (tonal, lexical-tone, cite Adoumacho et al. 2020).
sources.venue: Sound archives: a guide to their establishment and development

sources.note: §3 'Les tons' (pp. 8-10) states three phonemic level tones (high, mid, low), contour tones analysed as sequences of level tones, long level tones as tone sequences; tonal minimal triplet kú/kū/kù and further minimal pairs; orthography writes all tones (circumflex = H, diaeresis = M, unmarked = L); §3.2: tone on the verb marks perfective aspect, negation and future (grammatical tone), with examples; authors call for further study of grammatical tone.
